If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want to create a toy car model. Create a box with dimensions 200x100x100(X,Y,Z) as the body. The windshield can be created by subtracting a 50x100x50 block from an upper edge of the box. Add four wheels with a radius of 25 and a thickness of 10: Place two at (25,0,0) and (175,0,0) facing in the Y-Axis (0,1,0), and two at (25,100,0) and (175,100,0) facing in the negative Y-Axis (0,-1,0). | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation outline (using function calls only)

1. Body of the toy car  
   • Call functions.block with one block of size  
     x_size = [200], y_size = [100], z_size = [100]  
     Positioned at the global origin → x = [0], y = [0], z = [0]  
     subtraction = [False] (this establishes the solid body).

2. Windshield cut-out  
   • Call functions.block again, this time to subtract the windshield volume.  
     Use a block of size  
     x_size = [50], y_size = [100], z_size = [50]  
     Place its basepoint at the front-upper edge of the body → x = [0], y = [0], z = [50]  
     subtraction = [True] so it removes that volume.

3. Wheels (four cylinders)  
   All wheels have radius = 25 and thickness = 10, so their axial vectors are 10 mm long.  
   Cylinder arrays will therefore contain four entries each:

   • Base-center coordinates  
     baseCenterX = [25, 175, 25, 175]  
     baseCenterY = [ 0, 0, 100, 100]  
     baseCenterZ = [25, 25, 25, 25]

   • Axial direction/length (height vectors)  
     – Wheels at Y = 0 point along +Y (into the body): (0, 10, 0)  
     – Wheels at Y = 100 point along −Y (into the body): (0, −10, 0)  
     heightVectX = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
     heightVectY = [10, 10, −10, −10]  
     heightVectZ = [0, 0, 0, 0]

   • Radii, subtraction flags, functional tags  
     radius        = [25, 25, 25, 25]  
     subtraction   = [False, False, False, False] (they add material)  
     cylinder_func = [0, 0, 0, 0]  (normal geometry)

   • Call functions.cylinder once, supplying those four-element arrays.

4. Completion flag  
   • Finally call functions.finished with allFunctionsCalled = True.

This sequence creates the 200×100×100 body, subtracts the 50×100×50 windshield, and adds the four correctly oriented wheels.
